subject.title: fix(acp): preserve structured exec approval metadata

question: When a structured exec approval includes a `toolCallId` that has no unique pending match, should ACP retain the session-only fallback for a sole pending prompt, or fail closed whenever an identifier is present?
rationale: The current fallback preserves established delivery for early or incomplete events, but approval correlation is authorization-sensitive and automation cannot decide whether compatibility or strict identifier binding is the intended permanent boundary.

options.title: Confirm and test fallback
options.body: Approve the current compatibility behavior and add a focused regression test documenting the unmatched-id, single-pending path.

options.title: Fail closed on identifiers
options.body: When `toolCallId` is present, suppress the permission request unless it uniquely matches a pending tool call, accepting possible loss of early events.

options.title: Pause correlation change
options.body: Keep only the metadata propagation and defer identifier-based prompt selection until the ordering contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Confirm and test fallback
recommendation.body: Approve the current compatibility behavior and add a focused regression test documenting the unmatched-id, single-pending path.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged ACP approval relay and its existing session-correlation behavior.
